A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive Delay Model (ADM) study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable matching of equations, experiments, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic experiments and analyses of two- and five-region neural recordings in Section 4, plus GP-regression and visual-stimulus decoding results in Appendices D and H.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including neural-data comparisons, synthetic sensitivity experiments, regression results in Tables 1–2, and decoding results in Figure 10.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same GP-to-state-space construction, time-varying delay model, latent decomposition, and parallel-scan Kalman EM inference. No algorithmic component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios, V1–V2 recordings, five-region mouse recordings, GP-regression tasks, and visual-stimulus decoding task. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparators remain DLAG and MRM-GP in Figure 2, mDLAG in Figure 3, and DLAG, MRM-GP, and mp-srSLDS in Figure 9. Appendix D retains standard GP comparisons. The added Dowling citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The 0.8/0.1/0.1 training/validation/testing split, five-region cross-validation, latent dimensions, model orders, evaluation metrics, and Appendix D's 60/40 regression split are unchanged. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the same model-order analyses, sensitivity to region count, latent dimension and sequence length, latent-size misspecification tests, latent-activity visualizations, and decoding analysis. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The five-seed reporting in Section 4, five-run delay variance descriptions, plotted error bars, and uncertainty reporting in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. No new statistical procedure or run-count disclosure appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–10 retain identical numerical entries, plotted results, uncertainty values, and rankings. The accompanying qualitative findings also match, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions and equations are unchanged, including the covariance and Cholesky derivations in Appendix A, Kalman EM derivation in Appendix B, and kernel definitions in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and Discussion retain the same claims about the universal GP–SSM connection, continuously varying delays, and O(log T) scalability. Adding 'Brain' to the title makes the existing application explicit without changing claim scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of neural communication delays and experimental behavior remain unchanged, including appendix explanations. The limitations concerning cubic dependence on region count and model order, and proposed future directions, are also retained.

D1.justification: Both provide the same code-access link, dataset/session identifiers, preprocessing descriptions, hyperparameters, and implementation details. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v6 adds Dowling et al. (2021, 2023) to the Introduction's Markovian-GP discussion and bibliography. It clarifies that the cited multi-output approaches require spatial–temporal separability, while retaining the existing research positioning. Appendix I is unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 adds 'Brain' to the title and running headers and lightly rewrites the sentence describing earlier Markovian-GP approaches. The remaining narrative and section organization, including the appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer title and headers change their occupied space, while added citations and references cause limited text reflow on pages 2–3 and 9–10. One new reference has a malformed accent. All figures and tables retain identical formatting, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v6 modestly improves clarity and attribution by explicitly identifying brain communications in the title and acknowledging two additional studies in the existing Markovian-GP comparison. The scientific evidence and limitations, including all appendices, remain unchanged. A small typesetting defect in one new reference slightly reduces the presentation benefit.
